Wordsworth: Five Poems

华兹华斯诗五首 · 逐行对照 · 逐句批注

William Wordsworth

1798–18245 首逐行对照218 条批注

Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey (1798) · The Tables Turned (1798) · Nutting (1798/1800) · Lines Written in Early Spring (1798) · To the Torrent at the Devil's Bridge, North Wales (1824)。左栏英文原文，右栏逐行中文；每一诗段之后为该段的逐句批注（写作手法、词语、意象、表达效果），全书末为五首诗的整体解析。

Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey, On Revisiting the Banks of the Wye during a Tour. July 13, 1798丁登寺：旅途中重访怀河两岸时，在寺上游数英里处所作，1798年7月13日

Five years have past; five summers, with the length五年过去了；五个夏天，连同
Of five long winters! and again I hear五个漫长冬天的长度！我又一次听见
These waters, rolling from their mountain-springs这些流水，从它们的山泉里奔来，
With a soft inland murmur.—Once again带着一种柔和的内陆的低语。——再一次
Do I behold these steep and lofty cliffs,我望见这些陡峭而高耸的崖壁，
That on a wild secluded scene impress它们把更深的幽僻的思绪，印在
Thoughts of more deep seclusion; and connect这一片荒野而僻静的景色上；并且把
The landscape with the quiet of the sky.这风景与天空的静谧连结起来。
The day is come when I again repose那一天来到了，我又一次歇息在
Here, under this dark sycamore, and view这里，在这株幽暗的悬铃木下，观看
These plots of cottage-ground, these orchard-tufts,这些农舍的园地，这些成簇的果园，
Which at this season, with their unripe fruits,它们在这个季节里，带着未熟的果实，
Are clad in one green hue, and lose themselves披着同一种绿色，把自己隐没在
'Mid groves and copses. Once again I see树丛与矮林之间。我再一次看见
These hedge-rows, hardly hedge-rows, little lines这些树篱，几乎算不上树篱，只是一道道
Of sportive wood run wild: these pastoral farms,疯长的、嬉戏的林木：这些牧野的农庄，
Green to the very door; and wreaths of smoke一直绿到门前；还有一缕缕炊烟
Sent up, in silence, from among the trees!从树木之间，静静地升起！
With some uncertain notice, as might seem带着某种不确定的消息，仿佛来自
Of vagrant dwellers in the houseless woods,无屋的林中那些流浪的居住者，
Or of some Hermit's cave, where by his fire或某个隐士的洞穴，在那里，隐士
The Hermit sits alone.独自坐在他的火边。
批注 · Annotations
Five years have past; five summers开篇不以场景而以计数起句。past 是 passed 的旧式拼法。分号把"五年"这一抽象量度与"五个夏天"这一可感经验并置，随即由 five 的三次重复（five years / five summers / five long winters）形成 anaphora（首语重复），把时间量词念成近乎咒语的节拍。
with the length / Of five long winters关键的 enjambment（跨行）：length 悬在行末，读者要跨到下一行才等到 of five long winters，行的物理长度于是模仿了冬天的漫长。诗人不说"五年"而分拆成夏与冬，是把客观年份换算成主观受苦的刻度。
and again I hearagain 是全诗的母题词，此处第一次出现，后文 Once again、again 反复回响。值得注意的是重访先诉诸听觉而非视觉——水声先到，崖壁后到，符合人接近山谷的实际次序。
These waters, rolling from their mountain-springsThese 这一指示词（deictic）把读者硬拉到说话人身旁：不是"那些水"，是"这些水"，暗示诗人正站在现场。rolling 用现在分词，使流动成为持续状态而非一次动作。
With a soft inland murmur地理上的精确：Wye 河在此处仍是淡水，尚未受潮汐影响，故声音是 inland（内陆的）而非海口的喧响。华兹华斯自注提到过潮水影响的界限。murmur 属听觉，且是低音量的，与第二段城市的 din（喧嚣）形成远距离对照。
—Once again破折号造成句中 caesura（行中停顿），把行切成两半；blank verse（素体诗，无韵抑扬格五音步）正是靠这种句读与诗行错位来避免单调。Once again 起句而句子未完，推向下一行的倒装。
Do I behold these steep and lofty cliffs倒装（Do I behold 而非 I behold）使动词提前，带出仪式般的语气。behold 比 see 更重：含庄严注视、近乎瞻仰之意，为后文把风景抬升为宗教性对象埋下语调。
on a wild secluded scene impress / Thoughts of more deep seclusionimpress 一语双关：既是物理的"压印/刻印"，又是心理的"给人印象"，恰好跨在客体与主体之间——这正是全诗要论证的知觉模式。景物 secluded，思绪却"更深地" secluded，同源词的递进说明心灵把外物再加深一层。
and connect / The landscape with the quiet of the skyconnect 是全段的枢纽动词：崖壁的功能不是遮挡而是缝合。quiet 本为听觉词，却用来形容天空这一视觉对象，是 synaesthesia（通感）的轻微用法，也预告第二段"被安静下来的眼睛"。
The day is come when I again reposeThe day is come 用旧式的 be 完成体，语气近于圣经，带来"期盼已久之日终于来到"的分量。repose 比 rest 更正式，含"安放、托付"之意，暗示身体被景色接纳，而不只是歇脚。
under this dark sycamore, and viewdark 不是阴郁而是树荫浓密造成的暗，是触觉/温度感与视觉的合成。this 再次是现场指示词。诗人被安置在一个固定视点（树下），此后一切都是从这一点望出去的取景。
These plots of cottage-ground, these orchard-tufts连用两个 these 的排比，像目光逐格扫过。所看见的全是人经营过的土地——农舍菜地、果园——说明此处的"自然"从一开始就是人居其中的风景，而非荒野。tufts 一词把果树写成一簇簇的绒团，是俯瞰的远景视角。
Are clad in one green hue, and lose themselvesclad（着衣）是轻度 personification（拟人）。one green hue 精确对应"果实未熟"这一时令：颜色尚未分化，所以人工的界线也随之消失。lose themselves 主动语态，是果园自己隐没，而非被遮蔽。
'Mid groves and copses'Mid 是 amid 的省音诗体形式，撇号标出被削去的音节，为的是保住五音步的节拍——这类古语/诗歌用语（还有后文的 burthen、thro'）在 1798 年的语境里仍属可接受的诗语，与《抒情歌谣集》宣称的"日常语言"之间存在张力。
These hedge-rows, hardly hedge-rows著名的自我修正（self-correction）：先给出名词，立刻收回。这种"以否定来重新定义"的句法是华兹华斯的标志动作，效果是让读者目睹知觉在当场调整，比直接给出准确说法更有真实感。
little lines / Of sportive wood run wild树篱本是人划的界线，如今疯长成 sportive（嬉戏的）林木，人工与自然的分界正在被抹去——这与上文 lose themselves 是同一个动作的重复。lines 一词又暗指诗行本身（诗题即 Lines），一说这里有自指的双关。
Green to the very doorvery 加强"一直到门口"的极限位置。绿意逼近人的住所而不带威胁，是这一段风景伦理的核心：自然与人居互相渗透。极短的分句夹在长句之间，节奏上是一次呼吸。
wreaths of smoke / Sent up, in silence, from among the trees!wreaths（花环/盘绕的圈）既状炊烟的形，又带一丝葬仪花圈的余音。in silence 由两个逗号孤立出来，是听觉上的空白：全段唯一一处明确的"无声"。感叹号是段中第二个，标记情感的抬升，也是段落由描写转入猜想的转折点。
With some uncertain notice, as might seemuncertain 与 might seem 连用，把接下来的一切明确标为推测。notice 在此作"消息、告知"解——炊烟是一封读不清的信。此处诗人第一次承认自己在给风景添加内容，为第四段"眼睛半创造"的说法预先立案。
Of vagrant dwellers in the houseless woodsdwellers（居住者）与 houseless（无屋的）在同一行里互相抵消，是近乎 oxymoron（矛盾修辞）的搭配。历史语境上，这些"流浪居住者"很可能指当时聚居于 Wye 河谷的流民与烧炭人，晚近批评（如 Levinson）指责诗人把社会现实美化成风景。
Or of some Hermit's cave, where by his fire / The Hermit sits alone.以 Hermit 的重复收束，并让整段止于一个不足五音步的短行（The Hermit sits alone.），残缺的行长本身就是"独坐"的形式。隐士是诗人自身处境的镜像：一个独自坐着、观看火光的观照者——第一段于是从流水开始，以静止的人像结束。
These beauteous forms, 这些美丽的形象，
Through a long absence, have not been to me在长久的离别里，对我并不像
As is a landscape to a blind man's eye:一片风景对于一个盲人的眼睛：
But oft, in lonely rooms, and 'mid the din而是常常，在孤独的房间里，在市镇与
Of towns and cities, I have owed to them,城市的喧嚣之中，我从它们那里得到，
In hours of weariness, sensations sweet,在疲倦的时辰里，甜美的感觉，
Felt in the blood, and felt along the heart;在血液里感到，也沿着心脏感到；
And passing even into my purer mind甚至进入我更纯净的心智，
With tranquil restoration:—feelings too带来宁静的复原：——还有一些
Of unremembered pleasure: such, perhaps,记不起来的快乐的感情：这些，也许，
As have no slight or trivial influence有着并不轻微、也不琐屑的影响，
On that best portion of a good man's life,对于一个善良的人一生中最好的那部分，
His little, nameless, unremembered, acts对他那些细小的、无名的、无人记得的
Of kindness and of love. Nor less, I trust,仁慈与爱的行为。同样地，我相信，
To them I may have owed another gift,我或许还从它们得到过另一种赠礼，
Of aspect more sublime; that blessed mood,有着更崇高的容貌；那受福的心境，
In which the burthen of the mystery,在那心境里，神秘的重负，
In which the heavy and the weary weight在那心境里，那沉重而令人疲倦的重压，
Of all this unintelligible world,这整个不可理解的世界的重压，
Is lightened:—that serene and blessed mood,都被减轻了：——那澄静而受福的心境，
In which the affections gently lead us on,—在那心境里，情感温柔地引领我们向前，——
Until, the breath of this corporeal frame直到，这肉身躯壳的呼吸
And even the motion of our human blood以及我们人类血液的流动
Almost suspended, we are laid asleep都几乎停止，我们便在身体上
In body, and become a living soul:沉沉睡去，成为一个活的灵魂：
While with an eye made quiet by the power这时，凭着一只被和谐的力量、
Of harmony, and the deep power of joy,被欢乐的深沉力量所安静下来的眼睛，
We see into the life of things.我们看进了万物的生命。
批注 · Annotations
These beauteous forms段首缩进，接续上一段末行的残余音步，形式上表示"同一口气的继续"。forms 是关键词：诗人不说 scenes 或 places，而用带柏拉图色彩的 forms，第一步就把具体风景抽象为可被心灵携带的形式，为整段的记忆论作准备。
have not been to me / As is a landscape to a blind man's eye用否定的明喻来下定义——这是本段的基本句法策略：先说"不是什么"，再说"是什么"（But oft…）。盲人之眼的比喻极端而具体：不是"看不清"，是完全无用；跨行让 to me 悬置，否定要到下一行才落地。
But oft, in lonely rooms, and 'mid the din / Of towns and citiesBut 是全段的枢轴。lonely rooms（独处）与 din of towns（人群）是两种相反的城市苦境，都被列出，说明不是孤独或喧闹本身的问题。din 是刺耳的杂音，与第一段的 soft inland murmur 恰成听觉上的对位。
I have owed to themowe（欠、承蒙）引入一套贯穿全诗的债务—馈赠语汇（后文 another gift、recompense）。诗人把自己写成受惠者而非观赏者，风景是债主。这一经济学隐喻在批评中常被讨论。
In hours of weariness, sensations sweet形容词后置（sensations sweet 而非 sweet sensations）是拉丁化的诗体语序，让 sweet 落在行末重音上。sensations 是 18 世纪经验主义心理学的术语（洛克、哈特利），此处刻意用它，表明这份慰藉起于感官而非观念。
Felt in the blood, and felt along the heartfelt 的重复形成小型 anaphora，两个介词却不同：in 是浸没，along 是沿着流布，写出感受在体内扩散的路径。全句坚持把精神经验落在生理层面——血液、心脏——是本段最被引用的生理主义表述之一。
And passing even into my purer mindeven 标出这是一次越界。至此形成清晰的三级上升：blood → heart → mind，与哈特利的联想主义"由感官上升至理智"的阶梯一致。purer 是比较级，暗示心智比血液更"纯"，但并不否定后者。
With tranquil restoration:—feelings too冒号后紧跟破折号，是双重停顿：先宣告一个结论，又立刻补进第二样东西。restoration 兼有"恢复健康"与"复位、归还"两义，呼应上文的债务语汇。破折号在本段共出现三次，每次都在句子将要收束时把它撑开。
Of unremembered pleasureunremembered 不等于 forgotten：不是记住后又丢失，而是当初就未被记入意识。这一区分是华兹华斯记忆理论的要害——最有效的滋养恰恰是不经心留下的。此词稍后原样重现（unremembered acts），把自然的恩惠与人的善行系在同一个词上。
As have no slight or trivial influencelitotes（曲言法）：用双重否定来说"影响极大"。这种以退为进的说法与前面的 have not been to me、后面的 Nor less, I trust 一致，全段的正面主张几乎都是从否定里逼出来的，语气因此显得克制而可信。
On that best portion of a good man's life论述在此从个人心理转向道德。that best portion 用了一个悬念式的定语，读者要等下一行才知道"最好的部分"竟是些琐屑小事——这一延迟正是这句名言的力量所在。
His little, nameless, unremembered, acts四个修饰语用逗号一一隔开（连 acts 前都加逗号，是 1798 年版的标点），使节奏一顿一顿地慢下来，每个词都独立称量。三个形容词全是否定性的（小、无名、无人记得），价值恰恰由被剥去的东西来定义。这两行是全诗最常被单独引用的段落之一。
Of kindness and of love重复介词 of（不说 kindness and love）多出一个音节，把两个词分开称量，也补足音步。整个长句到此才落地：从"甜美的感觉"一路走到"仁慈与爱的行为"，感官经验被结算为道德资本。
Nor less, I trust又一次以否定推进（Nor less＝同样地、不亚于）。I trust 是谨慎的限定语——不是 I know。全诗在关键处反复插入这类保留（后文 I would believe、If this / Be but a vain belief），提醒读者这套自然信仰是被希望着的，而非被证明的。
another gift, / Of aspect more sublimegift 承接前面的 owed，赠礼母题第二次出现。sublime（崇高）是伯克与康德意义上的美学术语，与前文的 sweet、tranquil 属不同量级：那是慰藉，这是震撼。aspect（容貌、样态）把抽象的心境写得有一张脸。
that blessed mood用 that 而不是 a：仿佛这心境是读者已知之物，指示词制造出一种共同经验的假定。blessed 带宗教色彩，是全诗把自然经验语汇宗教化的一步；此语随即在六行后原样重现（that serene and blessed mood）。
In which the burthen of the mysteryburthen 是 burden 的古体拼法，多一个音节且音色更沉。the mystery 定冠词而不加说明，指的正是那说不清的东西——不可名状本身成了重量。这一短语在批评中被反复讨论，常被视为华兹华斯式"神秘"的关键定义。
In which the heavy and the weary weightIn which 的重复是 anaphora，句子在原地打转、迟迟不给主句动词，语法上的滞重模仿了它所描写的重压。heavy / weary / weight 三个 w 与重音节连成头韵，读起来必须放慢，是"以声达意"的教科书例证。
Of all this unintelligible world多音节的拉丁词 unintelligible 塞在一行单音节词中间，读起来最费力，正是"难以理解"的语音演示。all this 把范围推到极限：不是世界的某处费解，是整个世界。
Is lightened:—悬垂了整整四行的主语终于等到谓语，而谓语只有两个词——重负的解除在句法上表现为一次极短的落地。lighten 双关：既是"减轻"，也是"照亮"。冒号加破折号再次把句子撑开，让同一心境被重新命名一遍。
In which the affections gently lead us on,—affections 是 18 世纪心理学用语，指情感倾向而非现代的"感情"。lead us on 用被引导的被动姿态，主体交出主动权。行末的逗号加破折号使语句吊在半空，直接推入下一行的 Until——形式上就是"被引着往前走"。
the breath of this corporeal framecorporeal frame（肉身躯壳）是刻意生硬的解剖学式说法，与后面的 living soul 形成身/灵的对立。诗人坚持先把身体的机能一项项停掉（呼吸、血流），出神状态因此被写成生理事件而非幻象。
Almost suspended, we are laid asleepAlmost 是又一处限定：不是真的停止，诗人不愿把话说满。laid asleep 用被动语态（被安放着睡去），承接上文的 lead us on，主体始终是被动的一方。分词短语前置造成句首的一次停顿，节奏上像屏住呼吸。
In body, and become a living soula living soul 直接取自《创世记》2:7 中神吹气使人"成为有生的灵"，但华兹华斯把这一刻从造人的开端挪到了出神的顶点。In body 与 soul 在同一行内对峙，行中的逗号就是身与灵的分界。
While with an eye made quiet by the powermade quiet 是被动分词：眼睛不是自己安静下来，而是被和谐之力安抚。此处把第一段 the quiet of the sky 的 quiet 收回来用在感官上——外界的静被内化为观看的方式，与第一段 impress 的运作方向恰好相反。
We see into the life of things全诗最著名的一行，也是最有争议的一行。see into 而非 see：不是看见事物，是看进事物内部；things 用最朴素的词收尾，与上文的 unintelligible 形成对照。全行几乎全是单音节，在层层堆叠的长句之后显得异常清澈。一说这是泛神论的直陈，一说仅是一种想象状态的描述——诗人自己在下一段开头就用 If this / Be but a vain belief 收回了一半。
If this 如果这
Be but a vain belief, yet, oh! how oft—只是一种虚妄的信念，然而，哦！多少次——
In darkness and amid the many shapes在黑暗里，在那许多的形态之间，
Of joyless daylight; when the fretful stir那无欢的白昼的形态；当那烦躁的、
Unprofitable, and the fever of the world,无益的骚动，和这世界的热病，
Have hung upon the beatings of my heart—沉沉地压在我心脏的跳动上——
How oft, in spirit, have I turned to thee,多少次，我在精神里转向了你，
O sylvan Wye! thou wanderer thro' the woods,哦，林木的怀伊河！你这穿行于树林间的漫游者，
How often has my spirit turned to thee! 我的精神多少次转向了你！

If this / Be but a vain belief全诗最重要的自我保留：上一段刚宣称"看进了万物的生命"，此处立刻用条件句 if 与 but a vain belief（不过是一种妄念）为那一宣称加上对冲。诗人不撤回体验，只悬置其形而上的真值；跨行（enjambment，诗行未完而语意续接下一行）把 If this 孤悬行末，读者被迫停在"这"上一瞬，怀疑感因此先于内容抵达。
yet, oh! how oft—yet 把让步扭回肯定，oh! 的感叹与随后的破折号打断句法，使论证语气突然变成呼吸。how oft 起头却迟迟不给主句（要到第七行 How oft... have I turned 才落地），这段长悬垂句法正模仿了"多少次"的累积。

the fretful stir / Unprofitable形容词后置（Unprofitable 独占行首）是诗歌语用，也把"无益"从修饰语提升为判词。fretful 兼指烦躁与磨损（fret 原义为啃噬），stir 则是无方向的搅动——三词合起来定义了一种消耗性的、无产出的都市运动。

批注 · Annotations
And now, with gleams of half-extinguished thoughtAnd now 把时态从第三段的回忆性反复拉回眼前的此刻，是全诗第二次"现在"。gleams（微光）与 half-extinguished（半熄灭）都是光的隐喻，写记忆而非景物；重点是"半"——不是遗忘也不是重现，而是将熄未熄的中间态。
With many recognitions dim and faint三行连用 With / With / And somewhat of 的排比（anaphora，句首重复），把心理状态一层层叠加而不给主句，读者与诗人一同悬在辨认未成之际。recognitions 是认知性名词，比 memories 更强调"认出这是同一处"的动作。
And somewhat of a sad perplexitysomewhat of 的含糊量词与 perplexity 的抽象一起，刻意不把情绪说准。sad 在此不是悲伤而近于"惘然"，为整段"失而复得"的论证定下不纯粹的基调——欢愉里始终掺着损失。
The picture of the mind revives again悬垂三行后的主句，也是全段的启动点。picture of the mind 语义双关：既是心中所存的那幅画，也是心灵本身的图像；revives 用的是复活/苏醒之义，暗示它曾死过。此处景物已彻底转为心理事件——眼前的怀伊河谷只是记忆图像的显影液。冒号把这一句变成后文一切的总起。
While here I stand, not only with the sense / Of present pleasure全诗的三重时间在此并置：站立的现在、被复活的过去、下文的 future years。not only... but 的句式表明当下的快感本身不足为据，必须加上对未来的投资才构成论证。
That in this moment there is life and food / For future yearsfood 是本段第一个消化/营养隐喻，与后文 appetite、nurse、feed 连成一线：自然被当作可摄入、可储存的养分。此刻不是被享用而是被存进未来，把风景转成资本。
And so I dare to hopedare 泄露了不确定：希望在此是需要勇气的越界之举，而非自然的乐观。这一软化的措辞与第三段的 vain belief 一脉相承，是诗人反复给自己的结论留的退路。
Though changed, no doubt, from what I was when first / I came among these hillsno doubt 插入语（caesura，行中停顿）打断句子，语气近乎口语的自认。changed 一词是本段论证的枢纽：全段其余部分都在证明这一改变是获得而非亏损。
like a roe / I bounded o'er the mountainsroe 是欧洲狍，比 deer 更小更迅捷，明喻把少年写成不思考的动物。跨行把 I bounded 抛到下一行开头，重读落在动词上，读者的眼睛先跳一次行再读到"跳跃"，行的断裂本身模仿了弹跳。o'er 的省音使音步紧凑，全句轻快得不留反思余地。

Overview: A Thread Through the Five Poems总论：五首诗构成的一条线索

All five poems belong to the most productive years of Wordsworth's career (all but the last written between 1798 and 1800), and they repay being read together, because they keep returning to one and the same question: is the relation between human beings and nature a relation of knowledge, or a relation of morality? Wordsworth's answer always leans toward the latter — nature is not an object to be observed but a force that shapes the mind and the conscience.

这五首诗都写于华兹华斯创作力最旺盛的时期（除最后一首外，均在1798—1800年之间），可以放在一起读，因为它们反复处理同一个问题：人与自然的关系，究竟是一种认识关系，还是一种道德关系？ 华兹华斯的回答始终倾向后者——自然不是被观察的对象，而是塑造人的心灵与良知的力量。

But the five poems do not offer one answer; they offer a set of answers held in tension. "Tintern Abbey" claims that nature grants us a "sublime recompense"; "The Tables Turned" claims that books and science smother nature; "Nutting" instead admits that we do violence to nature, and suffers for it; "Lines Written in Early Spring" finds grief rising out of nature's own gladness; and the closing sonnet pushes nature back into a position of awe, something that cannot be domesticated. Read side by side, they show up the fissures within the Romantic conception of nature, rather than a single slogan about "returning to nature."

但五首诗给出的不是同一个答案，而是一组有张力的答案。《丁登寺》说自然给予人以"崇高的补偿"；《颠倒过来》说书本和科学扼杀了自然；《采榛记》却承认人对自然施加了暴力，并为此感到痛苦；《早春写下的诗行》在自然的欢乐中反而生出悲伤；最后那首十四行诗则把自然重新推回到令人敬畏、无法归化的位置。把它们并排读，能看到浪漫主义自然观内部的裂缝，而不只是一句"回归自然"的口号。

Three threads are worth following as you read: (1) the function of memory — how past experience is reactivated in the present and made to yield power; (2) modes of seeing — analytic looking versus receptive looking; and (3) where the moral conclusion comes from — in almost every one of these poems Wordsworth derives, from a landscape, a conclusion about how a person ought to live, and whether that derivation actually holds is exactly what these poems most deserve to be questioned about.

阅读时可以留意三条贯穿的线索：（1）记忆的功能——过去的经验如何在当下被重新激活并产生力量；（2）"看"的方式——是分析式的观看，还是接受式的观看；（3）道德结论从何而来——华兹华斯几乎每一首都要从风景推导出一个关于人应当如何生活的结论，而这个推导过程是否成立，正是这些诗最值得追问的地方。

1. Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey一、《丁登寺》

This is one of the most important poems in English Romanticism, completed on 13 July 1798 and placed last in Lyrical Ballads. The title itself is worth noticing: the poet is not inside Tintern Abbey but "a few miles above" it — the ruins are kept out of the field of vision, because what the poem sets out to write is not a religious relic but the way nature itself takes over the functions of religion.

这是英语浪漫主义最重要的诗之一，1798年7月13日写成，收入《抒情歌谣集》（Lyrical Ballads）末篇。标题本身就值得注意：诗人并不在丁登寺里，而在"寺上游几英里处"（a few miles above）——废墟被排除在视野之外，诗要写的不是宗教遗迹，而是自然本身如何承担起宗教的功能。

Structure: the poem's five verse paragraphs form a clear temporal syllogism. The first is the act of seeing in the present ("once again I hear / I behold"); the second and third go back to the five years of absence, showing how this landscape kept working on him while he was away; the fourth is the heart of the poem, setting the self he once was against the self he now is; the fifth turns to his sister Dorothy and entrusts his own experience to the next person. Note that this structure is not linear but a loop — present, past, present, future — and that loop is the formal embodiment of Wordsworth's poetics of memory.

结构：全诗五个诗段，构成一个清晰的时间三段论。第一段是当下的观看（"我又一次听见/望见"）；第二、三段回到过去五年的分离期，说明这片风景在他不在场时如何持续起作用；第四段是全诗的核心，比较"从前的我"与"现在的我"；第五段转向妹妹多萝西，把个人经验托付给下一个人。注意这个结构不是线性的，而是"现在—过去—现在—未来"的回环，这正是华兹华斯记忆诗学的形式体现。

Key passage one (verse paragraph two): "we are laid asleep / In body, and become a living soul: / While with an eye made quiet by the power / Of harmony, and the deep power of joy, / We see into the life of things." What is described here is something close to a trance: bodily activity all but ceases, and the person becomes, instead, "a living soul." The crucial phrase is see into, not see — not looking at things but looking into them. This stands in contrast to the "dissecting" mode of knowledge that "The Tables Turned" attacks: genuine insight comes from stillness and receptivity of the body, not from active analysis.

关键段落一（第二段）：'we are laid asleep / In body, and become a living soul: / While with an eye made quiet by the power / Of harmony, and the deep power of joy, / We see into the life of things.' 这里描写的是一种近乎出神的状态：身体的活动几乎停止，人反而成为"一个活的灵魂"。要点在于 see into，不是 see——不是观看事物，而是看进事物内部去。这与《颠倒过来》里被批判的"解剖"式认识形成对照：真正的洞察来自身体的静止与接受，而非主动的分析。

Key passage two (verse paragraph four): "That time is past, / And all its aching joys are now no more, / And all its dizzy raptures." This is the turning point of the poem. As a young man he ran through the hills like a roe, and nature was to him "an appetite," an unreflecting sensuous pleasure. That capacity is now gone. Wordsworth does not deny the loss — he says plainly that the time is past — but he claims there is an "Abundant recompense": he can now hear in nature "the still sad music of humanity." This is the step in the poem that most demands questioning: is what the loss bought maturity, or merely a rationalization of the loss? The poem is not entirely sure of itself either, which is why the third verse paragraph opens with "If this / Be but a vain belief." That "if" is the key to how honest the poem is.

关键段落二（第四段）：'That time is past, / And all its aching joys are now no more, / And all its dizzy raptures.' 这是全诗的转折。年少时他像狍子一样在山间奔跑，自然对他是"一种食欲"（an appetite），是不假思索的官能快感。这种能力已经失去了。华兹华斯没有否认这个损失——他明确说"那个时候过去了"——但他主张有"丰盛的补偿"（Abundant recompense）：现在他能在自然中听见 'the still sad music of humanity'（人性那静默而忧伤的音乐）。这是全诗最需要追问的一步：损失换来的是成熟，还是只是对损失的合理化？诗自己也不完全确定，所以第三段开头才会说 'If this / Be but a vain belief'（假如这只是一种徒然的信念）。这个"假如"是理解全诗诚实程度的钥匙。

Key passage three (end of verse paragraph four): "A presence that disturbs me with the joy / Of elevated thoughts; a sense sublime / Of something far more deeply interfused". This is the famous pantheistic formulation, but notice how careful Wordsworth's diction is: not "God" but "a presence," "something." He refuses to name it. Equally worth noticing is "both what they half create, / And what perceive" — the senses half create and half perceive. The line concedes that the nature he describes is in part a projection of his own mind. This is the central admission of Romantic epistemology, and the place where later critics (the New Historicists, for instance) have concentrated their attack.

关键段落三（第四段末）：'A presence that disturbs me with the joy / Of elevated thoughts; a sense sublime / Of something far more deeply interfused'。这是著名的泛神论式表述，但注意华兹华斯用词极为谨慎：不是"上帝"，而是"一种存在"（a presence）、"某种东西"（something）。他拒绝命名。同样值得注意的是 'both what they half create, / And what perceive'——感官"一半是创造，一半是感知"。这一句承认了：他所描述的自然，部分是他自己的心灵投射的产物。这是浪漫主义认识论的核心承认，也是后来批评者（如新历史主义）着力之处。

Questions worth pressing: the critic Marjorie Levinson made a famous claim — that this poem systematically erases history. The Wye valley of 1798 was no tranquil pastoral place; there was industry there, there were charcoal kilns, there were homeless vagrants. The "wreaths of smoke / Sent up, in silence" in the poem may well have come from charcoal burners, yet the poet imagines it as the fire of a "Hermit." From this you can go on to ask: is turning social suffering into landscape an evasion, or the inevitable price of Romantic aesthetics?

可以追问的问题：批评家 Marjorie Levinson 有一个著名论断——这首诗系统地"抹除"了历史。1798年的怀河谷地并非宁静的牧歌之地，那里有工业、有炭窑、有无家可归的流浪者。诗中那"静静升起的炊烟"，很可能来自烧炭工人；诗人却把它想象成"隐士"的火。你可以据此追问：这种把社会苦难转化为风景的做法，是逃避，还是浪漫主义美学的必然代价？

2. The Tables Turned二、《颠倒过来》The Tables Turned

In complete contrast to the meditative tone of "Tintern Abbey", this poem is short, colloquial, almost shouted: 'Up! up! my Friend, and quit your books!' It forms a pair with "Expostulation and Reply", and taken together the two poems stage a debate about where knowledge comes from. What follows works through the requirements of the class close-reading activity point by point.

与《丁登寺》的沉思语调完全相反，这首诗短促、口语化、几乎是喊出来的：'Up! up! my Friend, and quit your books!' 它与《劝诫与回答》（Expostulation and Reply）是一对，两首合起来是一场关于知识从何而来的辩论。下面按课堂 close reading 活动的要求逐项展开。

Question 1: How does the rhyme scheme relate to the poem's message?课堂问题一：韵律与诗的主张有什么关系？

The poem is written in the ballad stanza: tetrameter alternating with trimeter, rhyming abab. This was the format of oral song — something people who could not read could still remember and sing. To use a form that "circulates without books" in order to argue that we should put our books down is to make the form itself part of the argument. Wordsworth uses it again and again in Lyrical Ballads precisely in order to pull poetry out of the register of the study.

全诗用的是 ballad stanza（民谣体四行诗）：四音步与三音步交替，abab 交叉韵。这本是口传歌谣的格式——不识字的人也能记住、能唱。用这种"不需要书本就能流传"的形式来主张"放下书本"，形式本身就是论点的一部分。华兹华斯在《抒情歌谣集》里反复使用它，正是为了让诗脱离书斋的语域。

More telling still is the etymological distribution of the rhyme words. books/looks, double/trouble, head/spread, wealth/health, wood/good, Art/heart — these are almost all monosyllabic, everyday English words. The one polysyllabic, Latinate rhyme pair in the whole poem is intellect / dissect, and it falls exactly in the seventh stanza, the stanza that attacks the intellect. Phonetically, "intellect" and "dissect" are locked into the same sound; this ill-fitting pair of "foreign" rhymes sounds harder and more bookish than the words around it, so that the form carries out the argument on its own.

更值得细看的是韵脚的词源分布。books/looks、double/trouble、head/spread、wealth/health、wood/good、Art/heart——这些几乎全是单音节的日常英语词。全诗唯一一对多音节、拉丁词源的韵是 intellect / dissect，而它恰好落在批判理智的第七节。语音上，"理智"与"解剖"被锁成同一个音；这一对格格不入的"外来"韵，读起来就比周围的词更硬、更书面，形式自身完成了论证。

Two other rhymes are also doing semantic work: preacher / teacher fastens the woods to the church, letting the bird legitimately take over the office of preaching; linnet / in it is a nearly comic feminine rhyme that forces a colloquial phrase (on my life, there's more of wisdom in it) into rhyme with the name of a bird, demonstrating outright the claim that poetry should use the language people actually speak. And the short trimeter lines land almost always on an assertion or a rhetorical question ('Why all this toil and trouble?' / 'Than all the sages can' / 'We murder to dissect'), so that they read like the closing gesture of speech.

另外两处韵脚也在做意义的工作：preacher / teacher 把树林与教堂扣在一起，让鸟合法地接管布道的职分；linnet / in it 是一个近乎滑稽的阴性韵，硬把一句口语（on my life, there's more of wisdom in it）凑来与鸟名相押，直接示范了"用人们真正使用的语言"这条主张。而三音步的短行几乎总是落在断言或反问上（'Why all this toil and trouble?' / 'Than all the sages can' / 'We murder to dissect'），读来像口头说话的收束动作。

Question 2: What can nature teach that books cannot, and why is the argument both anti-scientific and pro-scientific?课堂问题二：自然能教而书本不能的是什么知识？为什么这个论证既反科学又亲科学？

Take first what he says nature teaches: 'One impulse from a vernal wood / May teach you more of man, / Of moral evil and of good, / Than all the sages can.' Note that what is taught is not natural history but moral knowledge — knowledge about man, about good and evil. And the means of transmission is an impulse (a momentary, bodily push), not a proposition. The fifth stanza states the character of this knowledge more plainly: 'a world of ready wealth' (wealth already lying there, requiring no mining), 'Spontaneous wisdom breathed by health' (spontaneous as breathing out). ready stands directly against toil in the opening stanza: book knowledge has to be bought with labour, while nature's knowledge asks only that you be present to receive it.

先看他说自然教什么：'One impulse from a vernal wood / May teach you more of man, / Of moral evil and of good, / Than all the sages can.' 注意教的不是博物学，而是道德知识——关于人、关于善恶。而传授的方式是 impulse（一次瞬时的、身体性的推动），不是命题。第五节把这种知识的性质说得更清楚：'a world of ready wealth'（现成的、不必开采的财富）、'Spontaneous wisdom breathed by health'（像呼气一样自发）。ready 与首节的 toil 正相对：书本知识要劳作换取，自然知识只需在场领受。

The anti-scientific side is stated flatly: 'Our meddling intellect / Mis-shapes the beauteous forms of things:— / We murder to dissect', and 'Enough of Science and of Art'.

反科学的一面很直白：'Our meddling intellect / Mis-shapes the beauteous forms of things:— / We murder to dissect'，以及 'Enough of Science and of Art'。

But the pro-scientific side holds just as well, and is the more interesting of the two. 'Come forth into the light of things' demands exactly that one face things themselves directly, rather than through the second-hand authority of books — which is precisely the slogan of experimental philosophy after Bacon (the Royal Society's motto nullius in verba, "take nobody's word for it"). 'a heart / That watches and receives' describes the posture of an observer. What he objects to, then, is not experience but the second step that works experience up into a system; the poem can perfectly well be read as a more thoroughgoing empiricism — one that refuses even the mediation of "system". You could push this in discussion as the point of contention: is "quit your books" against knowledge, or against authority?

但亲科学的一面同样成立，而且更有意思。'Come forth into the light of things' 要求的正是直接面对事物本身，不要经由书本的二手权威——这恰恰是培根以降实验哲学的口号（皇家学会的会训 nullius in verba，意即"不轻信任何人的话"）。'a heart / That watches and receives' 描述的是一个观察者的姿态。所以他反对的不是经验，而是把经验加工成体系的那第二步；这首诗完全可以读成一种更彻底的经验主义：连"体系"这一层中介也不要。你可以在小组里把这一点当作争议点来推——"quit your books" 究竟是反知识，还是反权威？

Question 3: Rewrite the seventh stanza in your own words课堂问题三：用自己的话重写第七节

Original: 'Sweet is the lore which Nature brings; / Our meddling intellect / Mis-shapes the beauteous forms of things:— / We murder to dissect.'

原文：'Sweet is the lore which Nature brings; / Our meddling intellect / Mis-shapes the beauteous forms of things:— / We murder to dissect.'

Paraphrase: The learning nature brings is sweet, and it costs no effort to come by; but our restless intellect, the moment it reaches out a hand, knocks things out of the shape they had. For our way of understanding a thing is to take it apart, and before it can be taken apart, it must first be made to die.

改写：自然带来的学问是甜的，不费力就到手；可我们那双闲不住的理智之手，一伸过去就把事物本来的形体弄走样了。因为我们理解一件东西的办法是把它拆开，而拆开之前，必须先让它死。

In rewriting, watch how the stanza is built on the distribution of active and passive: nature brings (gives), while we mis-shape, murder, dissect (do). Notice too the opposition of lore and intellect — lore is inherited knowledge, handed down by mouth and ear, while intellect is an analytic power actively applied; one is received, the other made by hand. Mis-shapes, likewise, does not mean "gets wrong" but "puts out of shape": the fault of the intellect is not an error of judgement but the fact that it has reached in and altered the form of its object.

改写时要留意这一节的骨架是主动与被动的分配：自然是 brings（给），我们是 mis-shapes、murder、dissect（做）。还要注意 lore 与 intellect 的对立——lore 指承袭的、口耳相传的旧知识，intellect 指主动施加的分析能力；一个是接收来的，一个是动手造的。Mis-shapes 也不是"弄错"而是"弄走样"：理智的过失不在判断失误，而在它动手改变了对象的形体。

Question 4: Why must you bring a heart rather than an eye?课堂问题四：为什么要你带来的是 heart 而不是 eye？

This is the most precise piece of word choice in the poem. The eye is the organ of scientific observation, and in this period the very byword for "objectivity" (the so-called innocent eye); to ask for the eye is already to have accepted the premise that observer and object stand apart. The heart governs feeling and body at once — it beats, it has blood in it — so that sending it to perform the act of watching amounts to demanding a kind of seeing that is not separated from feeling. He does not abolish seeing; he only forbids you to see with the eyes alone.

这是全诗最精确的一处选词。eye 是科学观察的器官，也是这个时期"客观"的代名词（所谓 the innocent eye）；一旦要求 eye，就等于先接受了观察者与对象相分离这个前提。heart 兼管情感与身体——它跳动、它有血——把它派去执行 watches 这个动作，等于要求一种不与感受分离的观看。他并没有取消看，只是不许你只用眼睛看。

The verb receives is just as crucial: knowledge is given, not gotten. An eye can frame a view, can capture it; a heart can only take what is given. Both verbs are purely receptive, and they reverse the driving gesture of the opening Up! up! from one end of the poem to the other — the poem chases you out of doors in order to make you stop.

receives 这个动词同样关键：知识是被给予的，不是被取得的。眼睛可以"取景"、可以"捕捉"，心只能领受。两个动词都是纯粹接受性的，与开篇 Up! up! 的驱赶动作形成首尾反转——诗把你赶出门，是为了让你停下来。

There is a further layer that is easy to miss: 'Close up those barren leaves' and 'bring with you a heart' make a pair. A book is an external thing, something that can be shut and left in the house; the heart is carried on the person and cannot be closed. The choice of organ is itself the conclusion.

还有一层容易漏掉：'Close up those barren leaves' 与 'bring with you a heart' 是一对。书是可以合上、可以留在屋里的外物；心是随身之物，无法关合。器官的选择本身就是结论。

Against the four claims of the Preface to Lyrical Ballads对照《抒情歌谣集》序言的四条主张

(1) Ordinary life is poetry's best subject matter. The scene of the poem is an evening, a field, a friend bent over his desk, and two ordinary birds — 'the woodland linnet' and 'the throstle' (the linnet and the song thrush, the commonest small birds of the English hedgerow), not the nightingale or skylark of the ode tradition. To choose a bird with no literary career of its own is itself a claim.

（1）日常生活是诗最好的题材。 全诗的场景是一个傍晚、一片田野、一个伏案的朋友，以及两只普通的鸟——'the woodland linnet' 与 'the throstle'（红雀与画眉，英国树篱间最常见的小鸟），不是颂诗传统里的夜莺或云雀。选一只没有文学履历的鸟，本身就是主张。

(2) Everyday language is the fittest language for poetry. 'Up! up!', 'Books!', 'on my life' (a street oath), 'Why all this toil and trouble?' — exclamation, swearing, spoken rhetorical question, with almost no poetic diction anywhere. The linnet / in it rhyme discussed above is the most direct evidence.

（2）日常语言最适合入诗。 'Up! up!'、'Books!'、'on my life'（市井赌咒语）、'Why all this toil and trouble?' —— 感叹、起誓、口语反问，几乎不见诗歌辞藻。前面说的 linnet / in it 那对韵是最直接的证据。

(3) The expression of feeling matters more than plot. Nothing happens in the poem; there is only a speaker persuading a friend, continuously. The one thing that does "occur" is the advance of the tone — from driving out (stanza 1) to description (stanza 2) to argument (stanzas 3 through 7) and back to a closing imperative (stanza 8).

（3）情感的表达重于情节。 全诗没有事件，只有一个说话人对朋友的持续劝说；唯一"发生"的是语气的推进——从驱赶（第一节）到描摹（第二节）到论证（第三至七节）再到收束的祈使（第八节）。

(4) Poetry is the spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings, and it takes its origin from emotion recollected in tranquillity. The first half of this has a literal counterpart in the poem: 'Spontaneous wisdom breathed by health' — spontaneous is exactly the Preface's word; 'One impulse from a vernal wood' is the instant of overflow itself. But the second half (recollected in tranquillity) does not fit — this poem is written out of a present impulse, with no distance of recollection at all. What really embodies the second half is "Tintern Abbey" (revisited and recollected only after five years). The incomplete fit is itself a good point for discussion: it shows that the Preface's four claims are not all present in every poem, and that Wordsworth's "doctrine" is realized through a division of labour across different poems.

（4）诗是强烈情感的自然流溢，起于在宁静中回想起来的情感。 前半句在诗里有字面对应：'Spontaneous wisdom breathed by health'，spontaneous 正是序言用的词；'One impulse from a vernal wood' 就是 overflow 的那一瞬。但后半句（recollected in tranquillity）对不上——这首诗写的是当下的冲动，没有任何回想的距离。真正体现后半句的是《丁登寺》（隔了五年才重访并回想）。这个不完全吻合本身是个好的讨论点：说明序言的四条并非每首都齐备，华兹华斯的"主义"是在不同的诗里分工实现的。

Microcosm: The Seventh Stanza as the Whole PoemMicrocosm：以第七节看全诗

If only one passage could be chosen to stand for the whole poem, choose the seventh stanza, and above all the closing half-line 'We murder to dissect'. There are three reasons, and the three are stacked on one another:

如果只能选一处代表整首诗，选第七节，尤其是结尾那半行 'We murder to dissect'。理由有三层，而且三层是叠在一起的：

Formally, it holds the only Latinate rhyme pair in the poem (intellect / dissect), which sounds abrupt in a poem written deliberately in everyday English — the poem uses sound to isolate, and let you hear, the very kind of language it is attacking. Propositionally, it is the tightest compression of the poem's argument: if knowing takes the form of taking apart, the price is the life of the thing known. In its self-contradiction, it exposes what the poem is gambling: a poem that announces that analysis is murder is itself an exquisitely worked product of craft — the strict metre, the pun (leaves are both the pages of a book and the leaves of a tree), the inversion (Sweet is the lore), the litotes (no mean preacher) are all achievements of "Art", and the Art in 'Enough of Science and of Art' counts the art of poetry itself among them.

形式上，它是全诗唯一一对拉丁词源的韵（intellect / dissect），在一首刻意用日常英语写成的诗里显得突兀——诗用语音把它批判的那种语言隔离出来给你听。命题上，它是全诗论点的最紧压缩：认识若采取拆解的方式，代价是对象的生命。自我矛盾上，它暴露了这首诗的赌注：一首宣布"分析即谋杀"的诗，本身是极精工的技艺产品——严整的格律、双关（leaves 既是书页又是树叶）、倒装（Sweet is the lore）、曲言（no mean preacher），无一不是"技艺"的成果，而 'Enough of Science and of Art' 里的 Art 把诗艺自己也算了进去。

Read as a microcosm of the whole poem, then, the stanza yields not an anti-intellectual slogan but a change of posture: not that one should stop thinking, but that one should change the way one keeps company with an object — from taking it apart by hand to stopping and receiving. And that change is one Wordsworth can only carry out by means of the very craft he criticizes.

所以把这一节当作全诗的缩影来读，得到的不是一句反智口号，而是一个姿势的更换：不是要人停止思考，而是要人换一种与对象相处的方式——从动手拆解，换成停下来领受。而这个更换，华兹华斯只能用他所批判的那套技艺来完成。

Reading alongside Hooke and White (General Question 2)与 Hooke、White 对读（活动通用问题二）

With Hooke: on the surface the two are flatly opposed — Hooke wants to extend the senses with an artificial organ like the microscope and see into the interior of things, while Wordsworth wants an unaided, direct encounter. But they share a deeper premise: both reject second-hand authority, both demand a return to things themselves, and both trace the failure of knowledge to some fallenness in man — for Hooke it is negligence and intemperance, for Wordsworth the meddling intellect. 'Come forth into the light of things' and Hooke's "rectifying the operations of the sense" are two versions of the same movement.

与 Hooke：表面上完全对立——胡克要用显微镜这样的"人造器官"延伸感官、看进事物内部，华兹华斯要不加器械地直接面对。但两人共享一个更深的前提：都反对二手权威，都要求回到 things themselves，而且都把认识的失败归因于人的某种堕落——胡克说是 negligence, intemperance（疏忽与放纵），华兹华斯说是 meddling intellect（多事的理智）。'Come forth into the light of things' 与胡克的"矫正感官的运作"其实是同一个动作的两种版本。

With White: White's journal comes closer than Hooke does to what this poem asks for. He records the weather and the phenology day by day, almost without theorizing, without conclusions, without dissection — 'a heart / That watches and receives' is very nearly a definition of how he writes. The difference is that White records numbers (barometric pressure, temperature, wind direction) and Wordsworth gives no number at all: 'One impulse' is a unit that cannot be measured. From here one can press the question: does White's recording count as the kind of receiving Wordsworth means? Or is it that, the moment you begin to record, you have already begun to dissect?

与 White：怀特的日记反而比胡克更接近这首诗的要求。他每日记录天气与物候，几乎不作理论、不给结论、不解剖——'a heart / That watches and receives' 差不多就是他那种写法的定义。差别在于怀特记数字（气压、气温、风向），华兹华斯一个数字也不给：'One impulse' 是不能被计量的单位。可以据此追问：怀特的记录算不算华兹华斯所说的那种"领受"？还是说，一旦你开始记录，就已经在 dissect 了？

Subjective and Objective (General Question 3)主观与客观（活动通用问题三）

The objective element: species and hours that are concrete and checkable — the linnet, the throstle, the vernal wood, 'His first sweet evening yellow' (evening light, not morning); the spatial relations of sun, mountain-top and green field are given clearly as well. The subjective element: calling the bird a preacher and nature She and teacher (personification); 'more of man, / Of moral evil and of good' is pure value judgement; 'Sweet is the lore' evaluates rather than describes.

客观的成分：具体可核查的物种与时辰——linnet、throstle、vernal wood、'His first sweet evening yellow'（傍晚而非清晨的光）；太阳、山头、绿野的空间关系也交代得清楚。主观的成分：把鸟称为 preacher、把自然称为 She 与 teacher（拟人）；'more of man, / Of moral evil and of good' 是纯粹的价值判断；'Sweet is the lore' 是评价而非描述。

The subtlest point of all is the Our in 'Our meddling intellect'. The speaker counts himself among those he criticizes — a subjective act of self-positioning, and yet exactly what makes the judgement seem impartial. Beyond that, the whole poem is addressed to a 'my Friend': it is private persuasion, not public argument, and the register alone declares its subjectivity.

最微妙的一处是 'Our meddling intellect' 里的 Our。说话人把自己也算进被批判者之列——这是一个主观的自我定位，却恰恰使论断显得不偏私。另外，整首诗是对一个 'my Friend' 说的，是私人劝说而非公共论证；语域本身就宣告了它的主观性。

What is 'unscientific' and what is 'experimental' (General Question 5)哪些地方"不科学"，哪些地方"实验性"（活动通用问题五）

What is unscientific: there is no data and no repeatability; an oath (on my life) stands in for evidence; a modal verb (May teach) stands in for a causal claim; the conclusion 'more of man than all the sages can' cannot be tested; and nature is personified as a teacher with a gender.

不科学之处：没有数据，没有可重复性；用起誓（on my life）代替证据；用情态动词（May teach）代替因果断言；'more of man than all the sages can' 这个结论无从检验；自然被拟人化为一位有性别的教师。

What is experimental: the insistence on first-hand experience, the demand that one leave the study and be there in person — which is exactly what divides experimental philosophy from scholastic learning; 'the light of things' is an appeal to things themselves. More importantly, Wordsworth uses the word himself: the Preface to Lyrical Ballads expressly calls these poems experiments, made to test whether the language of ordinary speech can become the language of poetry. So the poem is not merely "about" an experimental attitude; it declares itself the product of an experiment.

实验性之处：坚持第一手经验，要求走出书斋亲身到场——这正是实验哲学与经院学问的分野；'the light of things' 是对 things themselves 的诉求。更重要的是，华兹华斯自己就用了这个词：《抒情歌谣集》序言明确称这些诗为 experiments，用来测试日常语言能否成为诗的语言。所以这首诗不只是"关于"实验的态度，它自称是一次实验的产物。

3. Nutting三、《采榛记》

This poem is often set beside "Tintern Abbey" for comparison, because what it offers is the dark side of the same conception of nature. It recounts a boy's expedition into the woods to gather hazelnuts: the first two-thirds are a sensory abundance, and then the last twenty lines turn abruptly into destruction and remorse.

这首诗常被选来与《丁登寺》对读，因为它给出的是同一套自然观的阴暗面。诗写一个男孩去林中采榛子的经历，前三分之二是感官的丰盈，最后二十行突然转为破坏与愧疚。

Structure: by mood the poem divides into four movements — setting out (the comic outfit, the cast-off clothes, "more ragged than need was"); discovery (a hazel grove no one has reached before, 'A virgin scene!'); indulgence (lying on the mossy stones listening to the water, the heart "squandering its kindliness on things of no consequence"); and then violence and regret ('dragged to earth both branch and bough, with crash / And merciless ravage').

结构：可以按情绪分为四段——出发（滑稽的装扮，破旧衣服，"比需要的还要褴褛"）；发现（一处无人到过的榛树丛，'A virgin scene!'）；耽溺（躺在苔石上听水声，"心在无关紧要的事物上挥霍它的善意"）；然后是暴力与懊悔（'dragged to earth both branch and bough, with crash / And merciless ravage'）。

The key move: notice that the poem works from beginning to end with a sexual vocabulary — virgin scene (a sight untouched by any hand), voluptuous (given over to pleasure), banquet (the feast), and, at the last, deformed and sullied (marred and defiled). Wordsworth has written a childhood episode of nut-gathering as an act of violation. This is not over-reading; it is what the text itself keeps intimating.

关键处理：注意这首诗从头到尾用的是性的语汇——virgin scene（未经染指的景象）、voluptuous（耽于快感的）、banquet（宴席）、以及最后的 deformed and sullied（被毁损、被玷污）。华兹华斯把一次采集坚果的童年经历，写成了一场侵犯。这不是过度解读，是文本自己反复给出的暗示。

The two most important lines: 'I felt a sense of pain when I beheld / The silent trees, and saw the intruding sky.' After the destruction, the canopy has been torn open and the sky "intrudes." That intruding sky is an exceptionally precise piece of writing: the evidence of the violence is not the broken boughs but the sudden blank where there had been cover. Note the evasion built into the syntax: the intruder is plainly the boy himself, and yet grammatically it is the sky that intrudes.

最重要的两行：'I felt a sense of pain when I beheld / The silent trees, and saw the intruding sky.' 破坏之后，树冠被扯开，天空"侵入"进来。这个"侵入的天空"（the intruding sky）是极精确的写法：暴力的证据不是被折断的枝条，而是原本被遮蔽处突然出现的空白。注意句法上的推卸：闯入者明明是他自己，可在语法上，闯入的却成了天空。

The turn at the end: in the final three lines the poet addresses a "dearest Maiden" (usually taken to be his sister Dorothy) — move gently through these shades, and touch them with a gentle hand. This ending performs the same gesture as the fifth verse paragraph of "Tintern Abbey": handing on to the sister the lesson he has learned. The difference is that "Tintern Abbey" hands over a conviction, while what is handed over here is a warning. Hence the last line, 'for there is a spirit in the woods' — at once a consolation and a threat.

结尾的转向：最后三行诗人对一位"最亲爱的少女"（dearest Maiden，通常认为指妹妹多萝西）说话——请你温柔地走过这片树荫，用温柔的手去触碰。这个结尾与《丁登寺》第五段是同一个动作：把自己习得的教训转交给妹妹。区别在于，《丁登寺》交付的是信念，这里交付的是警告。所以最后一句 'for there is a spirit in the woods'（因为林中自有一个精灵），既是安慰，也是威胁。

4. Lines Written in Early Spring四、《早春写下的诗行》

The poem runs to twenty-four lines and its language is the simplest of any in this group, but its structure is extremely finely made — a closed circular argument.

全诗二十四行，语言是这组诗里最简单的，但它的结构极为精巧——一个封闭的循环论证。

The paradox of the opening: 'In that sweet mood when pleasant thoughts / Bring sad thoughts to the mind.' Why should delight in the woods bring sadness with it? The answer comes in the second stanza: because Nature links the human soul to her own fair works, and that contrast makes him think of 'What man has made of man'. In 1798, behind that phrase lie the collapse of the French Revolution, the war between Britain and France, and the rural poverty produced by enclosure.

开篇的悖论：'In that sweet mood when pleasant thoughts / Bring sad thoughts to the mind.'（在那甜美的心境里，愉快的念头把悲伤的念头带进心中。）为什么林中的欢乐会带来悲伤？答案在第二节：因为大自然把人的灵魂与她美好的造物连结在一起，而这个对照让他想到 'What man has made of man'（人把人变成了什么样子）。1798年，这句话背后是法国大革命的破灭、英法战争、以及圈地运动带来的乡村贫困。

The logic of the middle three stanzas: the poet observes the periwinkle, the birds, and the budding twigs, and three times draws the same conclusion — each of them is taking pleasure in its being. But notice that his phrasing weakens in certainty each time: in the third stanza it is 'tis my faith'; in the fourth, 'Their thoughts I cannot measure'; in the fifth, 'I must think, do all I can'. He knows perfectly well that this is projection, not observation. He holds to it all the same, but he marks his own unreliability.

中间三节的逻辑：诗人观察长春花、鸟、抽芽的枝条，三次得出同一个结论——它们都在享受快乐。但注意他每一次的措辞都在减弱确定性：第三节是 'tis my faith'（这是我的信念）；第四节是 'Their thoughts I cannot measure'（它们的心思我无法测度）；第五节是 'I must think, do all I can'（我怎么也不能不这样想）。他很清楚这是投射，不是观察。他仍然坚持，但他标注了自己的不可靠。

The ending: 'If this belief from heaven be sent, / If such be Nature's holy plan, / Have I not reason to lament / What man has made of man?' The two conditionals pick up the hesitation of the preceding stanzas, and the last line repeats verbatim the closing line of the second stanza. The whole poem returns to its starting point with nothing resolved. That refusal to close is deliberate: if the law of nature really is joy, then the suffering of human society has no natural warrant whatever — it is entirely of man's own making, and therefore all the less forgivable.

结尾：'If this belief from heaven be sent, / If such be Nature's holy plan, / Have I not reason to lament / What man has made of man?' 两个"如果"承接前面的犹疑，最后一句原样重复第二节的末行。整首诗回到起点，什么也没有解决。这个不闭合的结尾是有意的：如果自然的法则真是欢乐，那么人类社会的苦难就没有任何自然的根据，它完全是人自己造成的——因此才更加不可原谅。

5. To the Torrent at the Devil's Bridge, North Wales五、《致北威尔士魔鬼桥畔的激流》

Written in 1824, more than twenty years later than the other four, this is a poem of Wordsworth's late period, cast formally as an Italian sonnet (questions in the octave, a turn in the sestet). Read last, it lets you see what has changed in the poet's old age.

这首写于1824年，比其余四首晚了二十多年，是华兹华斯晚期的作品，形式上是一首意大利体十四行诗（前八行提问，后六行转向）。把它放在最后读，能看出诗人晚年的变化。

The octave: it consists entirely of questions — what is your name? From what height do you descend? Could such a force of water issue from a British source? Or is it Pindus (in Greece, then in the midst of its war of independence) that feeds you? Or is this the torrent of the Viamala (the perilous gorge in the Swiss Alps)? Standing before a Welsh waterfall, the poet keeps taking it for a river somewhere else. That misidentification is the crux: the scene before him is so overpowering that it exceeds the scale of native experience, and can only be named by borrowing foreign, sublime points of reference.

前八行：全部由问句组成——你叫什么名字？你从怎样的高处降下？这样的水力可能出自不列颠的源头吗？还是品都斯山（希腊，当时正在进行独立战争）喂养了你？或者这是维亚马拉峡谷（瑞士阿尔卑斯山中的险峡）的激流？诗人面对眼前的威尔士瀑布，却不断把它认作别处的河流。这种"认错"是关键：眼前的景象强烈到超出了本土经验的尺度，只能借助异域的、崇高的（sublime）参照来命名。

The turn in the sestet: 'There I seem to stand, / As in life's morn' — he seems to stand once more in the morning of life, seeing the woods rising in tiers, the snows that never melt, the sky that never gives up its calm. This is memory at work once again, structurally the same as in "Tintern Abbey," but briefer and more elderly: no long argument about moral compensation any more, only one brief return.

后六行的转折：'There I seem to stand, / As in life's morn'——他仿佛重新站在"生命的清晨"，看见层叠而上的树林、永不消融的积雪、从不放弃安宁的天空。这是记忆的又一次运作，与《丁登寺》同构，但更简短、更晚年：不再有关于道德补偿的长篇论证，只有一次短暂的返回。

The closing couplet: 'Such power possess the family of floods / Over the minds of Poets, young or old!' Note that final 'young or old'. It concedes the difference age makes, and at the same time claims that this power holds good across it. Read against "Tintern Abbey": the Wordsworth of 1798 needed dozens of lines to argue that the loss had been compensated; the Wordsworth of 1824 sets the question down in a single line. You may judge this to be genuine equanimity, or the exhaustion of the argument — both readings will hold.

末两行：'Such power possess the family of floods / Over the minds of Poets, young or old!' 注意 'young or old' 这个收尾。它承认了年龄的差别，也宣称这种力量跨越年龄依然有效。与《丁登寺》对读：1798年的华兹华斯需要用几十行来论证损失得到了补偿；1824年的他只用一行就把问题放下了。你可以判断这是真正的从容，还是论证的疲惫——两种读法都能成立。

Suggestions for Reading and Writing阅读与写作建议

If you are going to write a paper, here are several workable angles of approach. (1) Paired reading — "Tintern Abbey" and "Nutting" were written in the same period, one saying that nature gives, the other that man takes; setting the two side by side, you can argue that Wordsworth's conception of nature contains an ethical contradiction he himself never resolved. (2) Tracking a single word — "see" and its variants occur more than ten times in "Tintern Abbey," and the drift of sense from behold to see into to half create is itself a line of argument. (3) Historicizing reading — following Levinson's approach, ask after the social content that the landscape absorbs and disposes of in "Tintern Abbey" and "Early Spring" (the vagrants, the wreaths of smoke, "what man has made of man"). (4) Formal analysis — "The Tables Turned" and "Early Spring" both use the ballad stanza, which is Wordsworth putting into practice the claim of the Preface to Lyrical Ballads that poetry should use "the real language of men"; analyze how this "low" form is made to carry "high" propositions.

如果要写论文，几个可操作的切入角度：（1）对读——《丁登寺》与《采榛记》写于同一时期，一首说自然给予，一首说人索取；把两首放在一起，可以论证华兹华斯的自然观内含一个他本人未能解决的伦理矛盾。（2）追踪一个词——"see"及其变体在《丁登寺》中出现十余次，从 behold 到 see into 到 half create，词义的迁移本身就是一条论证线索。（3）历史化阅读——用 Levinson 的思路，追问《丁登寺》和《早春》中那些被风景吸收掉的社会内容（流浪者、炊烟、"人把人变成了什么样子"）。（4）形式分析——《颠倒过来》和《早春》都用民谣体（ballad stanza），这是华兹华斯在《抒情歌谣集》序言里主张"用人们真正使用的语言"的实践；分析这种"低"形式如何承载"高"命题。

When quoting, be alert to the question of text: the 1798 first printing of "Tintern Abbey" differs verbally from the revised versions of 1802 and 1815, and "Nutting" was not taken into Lyrical Ballads until the second edition of 1800. Specify in your writing the edition you are using.

引用时注意版本问题：《丁登寺》1798年初版与1802、1815年修订本有文字出入，《采榛记》1800年才收入第二版《抒情歌谣集》。写作时应注明所用版本。
